Section Officer

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for the Implementation of Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam (KNMT)

1. Introduction

In Tamil Nadu, there are 14 Corporations (except Greater Chennai Corporation), 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats. Many schemes taken up in the recent years such as Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT are aimed at improving the infrastructure facilities of Corporations and major towns alone. Smart Cities Mission is being implemented only in 11 Corporations. AMRUT is also being implemented in 28 Towns only. The coverage of schemes in Corporations is relatively high when compared to Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Hence it has been decided to introduce a new Scheme “Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam”’(KNMT) in all 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats so as to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in these Urban Local

Bodies. 2. Implementation Plan

The vision of the Government is providing water service connection to all urban house holds, safe sewer disposal to each household either through UGSS or through FSTP, street lights and good road facilities. Though there are schemes for the provision of 100% functional household tap connections, sewer links, roads, such are highly capital intensive, mostly covering only prominent areas in the Urban Local Bodies. Infrastructure gaps remain existing in many backward areas/ slums and also newly added areas of the Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Considering the above factors, it has been decided to give preference to the slum areas/ backward areas and added areas of the ULBs for the implementation of KNMT.

2.1 Urban Development Plan (UDP)

The distribution of basic amenities is not uniform across the Urban Local Bodies and in certain wards / specific areas, the basic amenities are still inadequate. In order to have an equitable distribution of basic amenities, a detailed survey will be conducted and an Urban Development Plan (UDP) will be prepared for each urban local body so as to assess the present availability of basic infrastructure and the gaps

to be fulfilled.

The detailed survey will be conducted ward wise, with respect to the availability of water supply, sanitation, internal roads, street lights,

burial ground / crematorium availability and other community infrastructure. With regard to roads, a detailed Roads Network Plan will be prepared indicating all the major roads maintained by various agencies viz National Highways, State Highways and Municipalities / Town Panchayats (Access roads and internal streets) in the Urban Local Bodies concerned. With respect to water supply, the total demand, including the present supply and the future requirement will be taken into account and incorporated. Based on this, a “City Water balance Plan” will be prepared for each Urban Local Body. Similar survey and assessment of the gaps will be undertaken for all needed components of the ULBs concerned.

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for the Implementation of Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam (KNMT)

1. Introduction

In Tamil Nadu, there are 14 Corporations (except Greater Chennai Corporation), 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats. Many schemes taken up in the recent years such as Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT are aimed at improving the infrastructure facilities of Corporations and major towns alone. Smart Cities Mission is being implemented only in 11 Corporations. AMRUT is also being implemented in 28 Towns only. The coverage of schemes in Corporations is relatively high when compared to Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Hence it has been decided to introduce a new Scheme “Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam”’(KNMT) in all 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats so as to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in these Urban Local

Bodies. 2. Implementation Plan

The vision of the Government is providing water service connection to all urban house holds, safe sewer disposal to each household either through UGSS or through FSTP, street lights and good road facilities. Though there are schemes for the provision of 100% functional household tap connections, sewer links, roads, such are highly capital intensive, mostly covering only prominent areas in the Urban Local Bodies. Infrastructure gaps remain existing in many backward areas/ slums and also newly added areas of the Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Considering the above factors, it has been decided to give preference to the slum areas/ backward areas and added areas of the ULBs for the implementation of KNMT.

2.1 Urban Development Plan (UDP)

The distribution of basic amenities is not uniform across the Urban Local Bodies and in certain wards / specific areas, the basic amenities are still inadequate. In order to have an equitable distribution of basic amenities, a detailed survey will be conducted and an Urban Development Plan (UDP) will be prepared for each urban local body so as to assess the present availability of basic infrastructure and the gaps

to be fulfilled.

The detailed survey will be conducted ward wise, with respect to the availability of water supply, sanitation, internal roads, street lights,

burial ground / crematorium availability and other community infrastructure. With regard to roads, a detailed Roads Network Plan will be prepared indicating all the major roads maintained by various agencies viz National Highways, State Highways and Municipalities / Town Panchayats (Access roads and internal streets) in the Urban Local Bodies concerned. With respect to water supply, the total demand, including the present supply and the future requirement will be taken into account and incorporated. Based on this, a “City Water balance Plan” will be prepared for each Urban Local Body. Similar survey and assessment of the gaps will be undertaken for all needed components of the ULBs concerned.

extracts.text:
Section Officer

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for the Implementation of Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam (KNMT)

1. Introduction

In Tamil Nadu, there are 14 Corporations (except Greater Chennai Corporation), 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats. Many schemes taken up in the recent years such as Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT are aimed at improving the infrastructure facilities of Corporations and major towns alone. Smart Cities Mission is being implemented only in 11 Corporations. AMRUT is also being implemented in 28 Towns only. The coverage of schemes in Corporations is relatively high when compared to Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Hence it has been decided to introduce a new Scheme “Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam”’(KNMT) in all 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats so as to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in these Urban Local

Bodies. 2. Implementation Plan

The vision of the Government is providing water service connection to all urban house holds, safe sewer disposal to each household either through UGSS or through FSTP, street lights and good road facilities. Though there are schemes for the provision of 100% functional household tap connections, sewer links, roads, such are highly capital intensive, mostly covering only prominent areas in the Urban Local Bodies. Infrastructure gaps remain existing in many backward areas/ slums and also newly added areas of the Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Considering the above factors, it has been decided to give preference to the slum areas/ backward areas and added areas of the ULBs for the implementation of KNMT.

2.1 Urban Development Plan (UDP)

The distribution of basic amenities is not uniform across the Urban Local Bodies and in certain wards / specific areas, the basic amenities are still inadequate. In order to have an equitable distribution of basic amenities, a detailed survey will be conducted and an Urban Development Plan (UDP) will be prepared for each urban local body so as to assess the present availability of basic infrastructure and the gaps

to be fulfilled.

The detailed survey will be conducted ward wise, with respect to the availability of water supply, sanitation, internal roads, street lights,

burial ground / crematorium availability and other community infrastructure. With regard to roads, a detailed Roads Network Plan will be prepared indicating all the major roads maintained by various agencies viz National Highways, State Highways and Municipalities / Town Panchayats (Access roads and internal streets) in the Urban Local Bodies concerned. With respect to water supply, the total demand, including the present supply and the future requirement will be taken into account and incorporated. Based on this, a “City Water balance Plan” will be prepared for each Urban Local Body. Similar survey and assessment of the gaps will be undertaken for all needed components of the ULBs concerned.
